citation.title: Charge exchange spectroscopy system calibration for ion temperature measurement in KSTAR

scope_read.limitations: Describes the 2010 initial system and calibration only. No plasma Ti profiles or uncertainties are shown. The 2022 chord configuration, fitting code and labels are not covered. Much of the text is future tense (planned 17-channel upgrade, NBI modulation).

claim_checks.proposed_claim: KSTAR CES measures the C VI 529 nm charge-exchange line with a separate background view.
claim_checks.source_finding: The bay M cassette views plasma and beam (active plus background). The bay A cassette views plasma only (background). Active and background fibres alternate at the spectrometer slit, alongside a Ne lamp fibre.
claim_checks.locator: p2 Abstract and Sec II; p3 Sec III, Fig 1 caption
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: KSTAR CES infers ion temperature and toroidal rotation from C VI (529 nm) charge-exchange emission, using a dedicated background view to separate active from passive emission [Ko2010].
claim_checks.qualification: This describes the 2010 instrument design. Background-subtraction performance is not demonstrated.

claim_checks.source_finding: Position calibration was done by back-illuminating fibres, with spot size under 5 mm (Fig 3). Wavelength calibration used Ne I lines near 528.0, 529.8 and 530.5 nm with Gaussian fits; the reported instrumental width is 1.14 Å (Fig 4). Absolute intensity calibration used a KRISS-calibrated halogen integrating sphere, performed before and after cassette insertion (Fig 5). The unshifted C VI reference is monitored shot by shot from edge background accumulation. In 2010, 8 of 50 fibres (R=1.7–2.35 m) were used: 10 cm spacing in the core and 5 cm at the edge. A 17-point layout was calibrated for a future upgrade. The listed hardware is a 1.33 m Czerny–Turner spectrometer and a back-illuminated CCD with 10 ms time resolution.
claim_checks.locator: pp2-3 Sec II; pp3-4 Sec III, Figs 3-5
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: The diagnostic is position-, wavelength- and absolutely intensity-calibrated using back-illuminated fibres, Ne I reference lines and a calibrated integrating-sphere source [Ko2010].
claim_checks.qualification: These results reflect the 2010 calibration, not the 2022 campaign. Whether the 10 ms CCD frame matches actual report availability is unknown.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: CES provides Ti from Doppler width on KSTAR.
claim_checks.source_finding: The paper states that ion temperature is derived from the CES spectra and gives the instrumental width. Only rotation is explicitly tied to Doppler shift. No Doppler-width formula, instrumental deconvolution procedure or Ti measurements are presented.
claim_checks.locator: p2 Sec I; p3 Sec II; p4 Sec III
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Ion temperature is inferred from the C VI charge-exchange spectrum, with the instrumental line width characterised by lamp calibration [Ko2010].
claim_checks.qualification: Cite a standard CES reference for Doppler broadening. This paper should not be cited as demonstrating Ti accuracy.

input_target_timing.outputs: Planned CES spectra yielding Ti and rotation per chord, every 10 ms
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: Calibration targets only; no comparison with independent Ti.

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Hardware time resolution of 10 ms (CCD) and an installed calibration chain
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Real-time Ti analysis, report latency, and fit runtime

forbidden_inferences: That the 2022 chord geometry or spacing matches the 2010 layout
That Ti labels are available online at 10 ms
That the planned 17-channel upgrade was in use in 2022
That the paper derives Ti from Doppler width explicitly
competing_or_complementary: Complementary: this is the provenance of the CES label instrument, not an estimator.
